fm.t: PSC Detention Prevention — Operational Field Manual
fm.v: v1.0 · 05 Nov 2026 · Paris MoU · Tokyo MoU · AMSA · USCG
note: Independent operational aid — not a PSC authority publication or a guarantee against detention. Ship-specific SMS, Flag, RO, maker manuals and port rules govern. Never falsify records, disguise defects, bypass interlocks or coach crew to mislead a PSCO.

Gabay lamang ito — hindi galing sa PSC at hindi garantiya laban sa detention. Ang SMS, Flag, RO, maker manual at port rules ang masusunod. Bawal ang pekeng record, pagtatago ng sira, bypass ng interlock o pagtuturo sa crew na manlinlang sa PSCO.
fm.grade: [A] critical / stop & escalate · [B] high risk / strong PSC trigger · [C] routine. PASS needs objective evidence. FAIL stays open until verified closed. N/A needs a recorded reason.
dec: Identify vessel and voyage
IMO / flag / type / age / last drydock / certificates / next port, ETAs and local rules.
Retrieve the actual record
Paris THETIS, Tokyo APCIS, USCG PSIX, AMSA via Tokyo; outstanding deficiencies and history.
Read red flags aloud
Any failed emergency, propulsion, fire, LSA, structural, navigation or pollution control is triaged immediately.
Review statutory validity
Original certificates, endorsements, survey windows, RO reports, conditions of class, extensions.
Run safe functional tests
C/E and Master supervise; manuals, permits, risk assessment, safe boundaries.
Verify crew competence
Show, do and explain on the actual equipment — no prompting, no rehearsed false answers.
Audit the paper trail
ORB/BWRB/GRB, maintenance, rest hours, drills, permits, passage plans, cargo, wages, complaints.
Resolve every open finding
Defect log, safety impact, owner, temporary safeguards, Flag/Class/port notification, closure proof.
Make a go/no-go decision
Master + C/E + Company, documented and conservative — never trade safety for ETA.
Meet the PSCO professionally
Single escort, valid documents, tested systems, accurate answers, log every observation.
fm.rule: A clean binder cannot rescue an unsafe ship. A functioning ship without honest, traceable evidence can still attract serious findings. Both are required.
ladder: Record / rectify in approved time / verify closure
Clear grounds / operational or statutory deficiency
Notify Master + Company; authority guidance; corrective plan before use
Immediate danger, serious pollution, cannot sail safely
Stop the operation; Master + DPA/Technical + Flag/RO/port; no departure until authorized
camp: Intelligence & standards: voyage profile, last 36-month PSC records and CAPs, RO items, survey status, drydock findings, near-misses, national notices, local entry/ballast/emission rules. Assign owner and focal points.

Real technical assurance: compartment-by-compartment inspection, safe alarm/actuator tests, spares and service agents, independent cross-check of safety-critical gear, find 'works only after reset' faults.
Verifiable completion: close findings with test, photo, PMS job card, signed notes, updated defect log; bridge/engine walkthroughs; crew practical questions; Class/Flag approvals actually issued.

High-risk re-check: re-test failed equipment, emergency gear, machinery alarms, escapes, firefighting; cargo plans, pilot transfer, passage plan, ballast plan, US/Australian reporting deadlines; readiness meeting.
Final walk-round: gangway, freeboard, hatch covers, deck oil, fire doors, emergency gear; known defects and declarations; evidence binder and officer assignments.
Welcome, single escort, safety boundaries; no unsupervised high-energy tests; documents promptly; demonstrate safely; record every question; seek written record.
Classify findings, root cause, sustainable CAPA, close with evidence and authority acceptance, share fleet lessons.
fm.m2s: Never let the shore office discover a critical failed system from the PSCO. Early notification and truthful engagement are signs of control, not weakness.

fm.ext: AMSA Marine Notice 2026/01: a certificate extension does not by itself legitimise continued commercial trading. It must follow the Convention provision and the voyage-to-survey limits — otherwise detention and possible RO attribution. [R16]

ch.stop: Expired critical certificate; unapproved exemption; open class condition affecting seaworthiness; invalid extension.
i: SOLAS/Load Line/IOPP/ISPP/IAPP/ISSC/SMC and relevant documents valid for ship and service
Endorsed dates, annexes, surveys, applicability matrix
RO conditions/recommendations and Flag dispensations reconciled with physical status
Current RO portal + written status; no undocumented overdue issue
Extensions checked under actual legal basis and voyage route
Flag/RO letter plus voyage and survey port matching conditions
Minimum Safe Manning vs actual crew by rank, licence, medical and STCW
Manning doc, endorsements, certificates, crew roster
DOC/SMC, MLC/DMLC, financial security, insurer evidence verified
Approved stability data and loading instrument certificates/access
Loading booklet, test evidence, software version
BWM certificate, approved BWMP, record book, BWMS documents
Ship radio certificate/licence, GMDSS documents, equipment inventory
Record of Equipment, logs, shore-based maintenance
CSR, registry and name/IMO/class particulars consistent
Full CSR trail and valid registration
Mandatory publications, correction services and charts updated
Documents organised with controlled originals and true translations
Index with holder and last verification date
Survey due dates and statutory windows checked 6 months forward
how: Pick three documents at random: issue → endorsement → annex → actual installation.
Ask the Master which conditions are outstanding; compare with the RO portal.
Reconcile certificate names, numbers and equipment inventory with fitted appliances.

ch.tf: ISM, PMS at pamamahala ng sira
ch.stop: Concealed critical defect; recurrent defect with no root-cause action; unapproved bypass of safety equipment.
i: All safety-critical defects known to Master/C/E and reported through SMS
Open defect register and reporting trail
No overdue safety-critical PMS tasks without risk assessment and approved mitigation
Defects needing Flag/RO/PSC notification have been notified
Corrective actions include effectiveness check, not just 'closed'
Critical spares and service vendors available
Drills meaningful, debriefed and linked to gaps
Risk assessments and permits match actual work
Safety meeting actions closed or tracked
Management of change effective after retrofit/repair
Procedures reflect current maker and Flag/RO guidance
DPA reachable, escalation channel posted and understood
Ship/shore communications include response time and resources
Third-party service reports accepted only after function verified
Post-service test witnessed by ship staff
how: Pick one previous PSC finding — does recurrence prevention actually work?
Ask a junior watchkeeper what happens when an essential alarm fails.
Compare PMS 'done' records with counters/readings and actual condition.

ch.stop: Invalid route or missing critical ENC; unsafe XTD/safety contour; non-functional vital bridge sensor without approved measures.
i: Berth-to-berth plan authorised, incl. pilotage and contingency
ECDIS route checked on largest scale with hazards and UKC
Route check log, traced high-risk legs, ENC corrections
XTD limits reasonable for channel, obstructions, manoeuvring
Safety depth/contour from draft, squat, tide, UKC and policy
Calculation sheet; settings and alarm validation
ENC permits and corrections current for route and backups
Update record, permit expiry, backup plan
GNSS, radars, echo sounder and heading cross-checked
Bridge test log, differences within limits
Radars, ARPA, AIS and target acquisition working
GMDSS tests and distress equipment serviceable
BNWAS, VDR/S-VDR, nav lights and whistle
Real test / annual VDR performance test
Standing orders, Master call criteria, restricted visibility explained
Position fixing and parallel indexing practical
Pilot exchange and briefing contain local hazards
how: Ask the OOW to show the next port approach and explain XTD near a critical obstruction.
Compare route-alarm handling with the SMS and past near-misses.
Observe live chart-correction status and backup ECDIS readiness.

ch.stop: Inoperable fixed firefighting; impaired fire main; fire detection disabled in a vital zone; compromised ER boundary.
i: Fixed CO2/foam/water-mist ready with correct controls and seals
Service report, control cabinet, maker confirmation
Fire main pressure and emergency fire pump demonstrable
Fire doors self-close, latch, no illegal hold-open devices
Fire detection panel free of faults; detectors functional
Fire dampers, vent stops and fuel QCVs accessible
ER escape routes free; doors, steps, lighting usable
Fireman's outfits, SCBA pressure and spare cylinders
Fire control plan current, displayed, duplicates available
Remote stops for pumps/fans labelled and functional
Detection zones and alarm audibility verified
Fire stations, routes and instructions legible
how: Test representative fire doors on each deck, including those used most.
Ask the 3/E to trace emergency fire pump suction and operation.
Never discharge fixed agent to 'show it works' — use approved test methods.

ch.stop: Unsafe hook/release; required lifeboat unusable; muster alarm unserviceable; unsafe launching brake.
i: Lifeboat/rescue boat release gear free of unapproved modifications
Falls, hooks, winches, brakes, limit switches serviceable
Embarkation arrangements, gripes, blocks and access correct
Boat engine, steering, communications, starting battery usable
Safe start per maker and local rules
Mandatory LSA inspections/service by authorised people in date
Liferafts secured, painter attached, HRU dates valid
Muster list matches crew and duties; understood
Rescue boat deployment risk-assessed, people competent
Emergency lighting on escape and embarkation routes
LSA spares and hydraulic fluids, no leaks
how: Open boats only in a maker-compliant safe configuration; never enter if release/securing is not safe.
Controlled engine start and alarm drill — no hazardous launch when conditions do not permit.
Cross-check annual/5-yearly service against SOLAS/MSC resolutions and equipment age.

ch.stop: Failed emergency generator; failed steering redundancy; machinery shutdown integrity impaired; unprotected hot oil leak.
i: Emergency generator starts and takes essential loads
V/Hz, transfer and load test record
Steering gear main/aux modes with bridge communication
ME/AE shutdowns, protective alarms, critical sensors
Alarm test sheet and known deficiencies
Bilge high-level and flooding alarms operate
Boilers, compressors, pressure safety devices serviced
Leaks, hot surfaces and insulation corrected
High-temp, oil-mist and crankcase protection maintained
Cable penetrations, emergency circuits, earthing sound
Cooling, fuel/LO changeovers tested where safe
Remote emergency stops and QCVs known
how: Witness emergency generator auto-start/transfer by an authorised method with contingency ready.
Observe the local steering test with bridge and engine crew.
Check repaired ME exhaust/turbo insulation for hot exposure and oil splash.

ch.stop: OWS bypass or manipulation; non-representative sample; failed alarm/stopping valve; records inconsistent with discharge.
i: OWS approved and piping matches approved drawings
Representative effluent flows to the oil content monitor
Genuine sample flow in recirculation test
Alarm and stopping device activate on high oil content
Clean-water flushing does not bypass alarm/auto-stop
Opening flush valve → alarm and stop (AMSA)
No unsealed bypass or isolated sample line while overboard enabled
Fail-safe on loss of sample flow / monitor failure
Test done in safe recirculation, not overboard
ORB reconciles with soundings, transfers, receipts
Sludge/bilge tank valves, soundings, level alarms
Officer demonstrates start, alarm response, shutdown
Discharge limits and local restrictions checked
No undocumented changes to 3-way valve or OCM sample pipes
Daily rounds include leaks, seals, alarms, sample line
how: MEPC.107(49) equipment: AMSA expects monitor indication ≤5 s and total auto-stop ≤20 s — apply to the correct standard.
Demonstrate the clean-water flushing interlock in recirculation, never real overboard discharge.
Never coach crew to conceal a bypass — preserve evidence and escalate.

ch.t: MARPOL IV, V, VI & pollution control
ch.tf: MARPOL IV, V, VI at polusyon
ch.stop: Illegal overboard discharge; disabled pollution control; missing mandated response capability.
i: Sewage system and discharge mode compliant with location
Oil/chemical leaks to sea prevented; scupper controls work
Garbage plan, segregation and GRB accurate
Annex VI sulphur compliance with ECA route and BDN/sample
Fuel flashpoint supplier declaration where required
EGCS records / washwater use per local rules
Bunkering SOPEP drills, drip trays, scupper plugs
SEEMP / DCS / CII data and verifier requirements
Pollution response contacts and SOPEP/SMPEP current
Ballast/pollution alarms and line isolation, no bypass
how: Trace five random ORB/GRB entries against operational records.
Ask crew where food waste, plastics and bilge water may legally go on this route.
Check national/local EGCS, sewage and garbage rules before arrival.

ch.stop: Unauthorised BWMS bypass; prohibited discharge; unreported US BWMS malfunction; no approved contingency.
i: BWMS in service, approved for the discharge, inside limits
Treatment bypass inhibited or under authorised procedure
No ballast release until local rules and approvals resolved
US: approved method and failure reporting to COTP
BWMP current; BWRB complete and consistent
Neutralisation / hold times / sampling per manual
D-2 biological compliance test requirement assessed
Australia DAFF and inter-port ballast checked
Crew explain BWMS alarm response and bypass prohibition
how: US: never assume ballast exchange alone is accepted instead of a required approved method. [R24]
Australia: verify Biosecurity Act/DAFF rules even with valid IMO certificate and BWMS. [R26]
No universal '300% overflow' rule — use the approved plan and local law.

ch.t: Hull, load line, hatch covers & bulk
ch.tf: Hull, load line, hatch cover at bulk
ch.stop: Hull fracture or serious wastage; ineffective hatch cover; uncontrolled water ingress; load line fraud.
i: Corrosion, fractures, wastage, temporary repairs investigated
Hatch covers close and seal; no unsecured cleats or major cracks
Weathertight doors and ventilator closures effective and marked
Load line marks and drafts legible and match certificate
Side shell, decks, frames, bulkheads, bilges checked for cracks
Hold bilges and suctions free-flowing, not leaking
Hatch hydraulics, pipes, retaining valves, stoppers sound
Ballast tank paint not hiding unassessed corrosion
Cargo ventilation closures / ducts dry and accessible
Access covers and cable passages sealed
Loading plan, stresses, trim, stability within limits
how: Walk one hatch cover with the C/O — find every drain, seal, cleat and stop.
Inspect bilge alarms and the last hold inspection record.
Master shows why draft/load line marks match the certificate.

ch.tf: Pilot ladder, mooring at deck safety
ch.stop: Pilot ladder dangerous; mooring winch brake unsafe; severe deck gear failure.
i: Pilot ladder / combination arrangement per applicable SOLAS V/23
Ropes, spreaders, steps, securing points, certificate/records
Hands-on inspection; no repairs to unsafe rope
No unauthorised shackles or improper securing
Mooring winch brakes tested per ship-specific MBL/SDMBL
Mooring lines/wires safe and tracked in the LMP
Line identification and LMP consistent with fitted gear
Anchor and windlass, stoppers, spurling pipes
Deck lifting gear tests and colour coding
Pilot and tug arrangements briefed with local rules
Deck hazard labels, surfaces, access hatches
how: Rig the ladder at a safe time and photograph it from the side.
Ask crew which strong points hold the pilot ladder and why.
Check any '60% SDMBL' brake setting only against approved ship/company guidance and OCIMF.

ch.tf: MLC, rest hours at kapakanan ng crew
ch.stop: Systemic falsification of rest hours; missing safe manning; crew unable to respond to emergencies; denial of wages/necessities.
i: Hours of rest authentic and meet STCW/MLC minimums
Timesheets vs logs, permits, cargo calls
Muster and safe manning maintained with competent watchkeepers
Wages and repatriation protection; financial security
SEAs valid; CBA and conditions accessible
Crew explain escalation and shore contacts
Medical supplies, log, equipment, officer competence
Drinking water testing and food storage temperatures
Rest records reflect drills and overtime
how: Cross-check two random rest-hour logs with cargo ops and mooring stations.
Ask crew privately how they report an unsafe order and whether they can reach the DPA.
Never brief crew to give rote false answers or change time sheets.

ch.stop: Crew cannot execute mandatory emergency functions; no gas monitor for enclosed space; cannot recover from blackout.
i: Crew knows individual fire/abandon duties on current muster list
Emergency steering and blackout recovery familiar
Fire and abandon-ship drills recorded and meaningful
Enclosed-space rescue plan, gas detection, rescue gear
Entry permits include measured atmospheres and monitoring
SCBA donning and casualty transport exercised
SSP, security levels and restricted areas managed
Security drills and duties up to date
Emergency shore contacts, spill response, reporting
Cyber/bridge system change control and backups
New joiners' familiarisation practical and signed
how: One unscripted tabletop scenario; ask junior crew to locate equipment.
Never use live CO2, hot work, energised panels or unsafe entry as a 'test'.
Enclosed space re-check frequency follows the ship-specific risk assessment — no universal 30-minute rule.

ch.tf: Para sa uri ng barko (bulk muna)
ch.stop: Operation beyond statutory endorsement; critical cargo protection unavailable; stability/stress breach.
i: BULK: hold water-ingress detection / structure after heavy weather
Alarm logs, hold inspection, hatch test
TANKER: inert gas and O2 control
TANKER: cargo pump stops, high-level, cargo alarms
TANKER: ODME and cargo record equipment
GAS: ESD, gas detection, cargo protection
PASSENGER: muster, crowd management, fire zones
CONTAINER: lashing computer, VGM, CSAP, stow limits
RO-RO: vehicle deck FFA, ramps/doors, securing
ALTERNATIVE FUEL: IGF systems and endorsements
how: Build a ship-specific applicability matrix before boarding.
Request cargo/terminal documents early.
Dangerous/pressurised equipment: maker procedures and authorised witnesses only.

tree: Is there actual danger to life, safety, seaworthiness, environment or welfare?
YES → STOP the operation, protect people, tell the Master. NO → next gate.
Is law/approval breached, a mandatory system inoperative or a certificate invalid?
YES → Company + Flag/RO/port; corrective plan before sailing.
Can the defect be safely repaired and retested before arrival?
YES → competent repair, witnessed test, proof. NO → contingency and authority decision.
Are crew using a prohibited bypass, altered settings or fabricated records?
YES → stop, preserve evidence, escalate; do not conceal.
Is closure independently verified, records reconciled, crew capable?
NO → stays OPEN. YES → document closure and readiness.
Has a regulatory control or detention been imposed?
YES → comply with the written direction; do not sail until released.
cases: Three doors wedged open; two fail to latch; crew: 'we close them for inspection'.
[A] Remove wedges, restore closers/latches, test all zones, find why it was tolerated, log, prevent recurrence. Fire/ISM and culture.
OCM receives little water while overboard position remains available.
[A] Prohibit discharge, inspect line and fail-safe, repair, retest in recirculation, notify as required. MARPOL I / ISM; AMSA focus.
UV sensor fails during cargo ops; crew plans exchange and later discharge in port.
[A] Stop prohibited discharge, verify legal method, notify COTP, get port instruction. 33 CFR 151 — exchange alone is no substitute.
3-month extension, but the ship keeps trading between unrelated load ports.
[A] Question validity, contact Flag/RO at once, verify voyage-to-survey conditions. AMSA MN 2026/01.
OOW sets 0.5 NM XTD in a narrow passage next to a submerged danger, no UKC rationale.
[A] Reassess leg limits and route before transit; Master approval; OOW competence retest. SOLAS V.
itin: Crew and voyage particulars; defect register; Class/Flag/port open items; recent PSC reports; stop-work orders.
ECDIS XTD/ENC, pilot ladder, nav lights, VDR, fire stations, hatch covers, mooring brakes/marking.
Fire doors and escapes, alarm points, LSA, muster, emergency stations, MLC water/food/rest.
Emergency generator + steering tests, fire pump, hot surfaces, OWS sample/15 ppm, BWMS and valves.
Hatch/hold condition, CSM, VGM/lashing, loading computer, ORB/BWRB, PMS, permits.
Independent interviews, firefighting tabletop, look-back at defects.
Grade every failure, owner, deadline, authority contact, no-go restrictions, spares/service actions.
nogo: All statutory certificates and extensions legitimately valid for this voyage?
Flag, RO and authorities informed of defects that must be reported?
Fire main, fixed FFA, detection and essential fire boundaries function?
Required lifeboat/rescue arrangements can be used safely?
Emergency power, steering and critical machinery protection function?
Next route safe on corrected charts and suitably set ECDIS?
No unlawful or manipulative OWS/OCM/bypass arrangement?
Ballast can be handled and discharged lawfully at every intended location?
Hull, weathertight integrity and hatch closures safe for the voyage?
Cargo stow/segregation/securing complies with approved plans?
Crew can execute duties at fire, flooding, blackout and abandonment?
Manning, rest and basic living/medical conditions actually compliant?
Pilot ladder and mooring systems safe for intended operations?
All critical defects physically closed or under authorised restrictions?
Master can truthfully explain every open item and the departure decision?
fm.ethic: Find the defect before the State does. Stop the unsafe operation. Tell the truth. Repair it. Prove it. Learn from it.

ca.t: Zero Deficiency Canada — PSC Walk-Round Guide
ca.v: Rev.0 · 03 Nov 2026 · by Capt. George Barbaris · Vancouver · Quebec · St. Lawrence
rule: Tick it — fix it — prove it. Anything you cannot fix on board: report to the office before arrival with a photo. A defect already reported with a repair plan is treated far better than one the PSCO finds hidden.

Tsek — ayusin — patunayan. Kung hindi maaayos sa barko: i-report sa office bago dumating, may litrato. Mas maganda ang trato sa sirang naka-report na may repair plan kaysa sa itinago na makikita ng PSCO.
rounds: Every line checked; defect list + photos to office
Open items + all ★ lines; drills done
Gangway, pilot ladder, fire doors, ER bilges, escapes, accommodation, certificate file
ca.see: Canada rules, whale zones, ballast, winter navigation and the real 2025 Canadian detentions are in 🛂 PSC → 🇨🇦 Canada.
ca.flags: ★ detention risk — must be 100% · CA Canada hotspot (Canadian rule or real 2025 Canadian deficiency) · ◆ ship-specific open item (from your private ship pack)
pre: Office
Download and review the ship's last PSC reports (especially any detention) — confirm every item closed; the PSCO sees the history.
Office
Close out the last RightShip report with before/after photos; send evidence before arrival.
Office
Close any class/flag dispensations in writing (e.g. rescue boat engine, VDR repairs).
Office
Crew contracts correct (right shipowner name, current class).
Office
Exemption certificates valid for the voyage; cargo on the annex list.
Office
Crew reliefs: nobody over 11 months on board at arrival in Canada.
Office/Agent
Canadian charts & publications list, ballast water report, pre-arrival notifications, garbage contractor, grain 'Readiness to Load' request to Transport Canada.
Office/Agent
Quebec/St. Lawrence Dec–Mar: confirm winter sea-water cooling compliance with Transport Canada (winternav@tc.gc.ca) and winter pilotage requirements.
Ship
Walk-round 14 days before arrival → defect list + photos to office; repeat 5 days before; golden-hour round on arrival day.
Ship
Drills from the drill list done and recorded before arrival.

why: The PSCO decides in the first 5 minutes whether this is a 'quick' or an 'expanded' inspection. Rust streaks, a sloppy gangway and no watchman = clear grounds to dig deeper.
Sa unang 5 minuto nagpapasya ang PSCO kung mabilis o expanded ang inspection. Kalawang, magulong gangway at walang bantay = dahilan para maghukay pa.
i: Safety net rigged full length, stanchions & handrails tight, steps not bent, lit at night, lifebuoy with line at the head.
Safety net buong haba, mahigpit ang stanchion at handrail, hindi baluktot ang baitang, may ilaw sa gabi, lifebuoy na may lubid sa itaas.
AB on watch with visitor log, ID check, ISPS level sign, ship particulars & 'No smoking' signs at the gangway.
May AB na bantay, visitor log, ID check, ISPS level sign, ship particulars at 'No smoking' sa gangway.
Draft marks, load line, IMO no.
Freshly painted and readable both sides; IMO number marking visible (SOLAS XI-1/3). Plimsoll mark clear.
Draft marks, load line, IMO no.
Bagong pintura at nababasa sa magkabilang side; kita ang IMO number (SOLAS XI-1/3). Malinaw ang Plimsoll mark.
No oil sheen, no garbage overside, no peeling anti-fouling. In Quebec 2025 a ship was detained after aerial photos showed AF paint peeling into the St. Lawrence.
Walang oil sheen, walang basura sa tabi, walang natutuklap na anti-fouling. Sa Quebec 2025, na-detain ang barko dahil sa litrato mula sa ere ng natutuklap na AF paint.
No leaking overboard valves; scuppers plugged during bunkering; save-alls/drip trays empty.
Walang tagas sa overboard valve; nakasaksak ang scupper habang bunkering; walang laman ang save-all/drip tray.

why: Canadian pilots (Pacific and Laurentian Pilotage Authorities) report defective pilot ladders straight to Transport Canada. A bad ladder = PSC on board before the pilot reaches the bridge.
Ang mga pilot sa Canada ay nagre-report agad sa Transport Canada ng sirang pilot ladder. Masamang ladder = PSC sa barko bago pa makarating ang pilot sa bridge.
i: Ladder certificate/ID on board, side ropes not worn, steps not cracked/loose, spreaders correct, no knots, shackles or splices, replacement record in log.
Certificate at kondisyon ng pilot ladder
May certificate/ID, hindi gasgas ang side rope, walang basag/maluwag na baitang, tama ang spreader, walang buhol, shackle o splice, may record ng palit.
Secured to strong points / securing points — never to handrails or stanchions. Steps rest firmly against the hull.
Nakatali sa strong point — hindi sa handrail o stanchion. Nakadikit nang mahigpit ang baitang sa hull.
Rigged at the height the pilot asks for. If combination: accommodation ladder max 45°, pilot ladder 1.5 m above the platform and secured to ship's side.
Sa taas na hinihingi ng pilot. Kung combination: accommodation ladder max 45°, pilot ladder 1.5 m sa itaas ng platform at nakatali sa gilid ng barko.
Handhold stanchions/bulwark ladder OK, lighting, lifebuoy with self-igniting light, heaving line, officer with radio attending, man-ropes if requested.
OK ang handhold stanchion/bulwark ladder, may ilaw, lifebuoy na may self-igniting light, heaving line, officer na may radyo, man-rope kung hihingin.
Helmet, lifejacket/work vest, gloves, safety shoes — company list posted at pilot station.
PPE ng crew sa pilot ladder
Helmet, lifejacket/work vest, guwantes, safety shoes — nakapaskil ang listahan sa pilot station.

why: Vancouver, July 2025: a ship was detained because the OOW did not know the ECDIS, echo sounder, gyro and Inmarsat. Familiarity is inspected, not only the equipment.
Vancouver, Hulyo 2025: na-detain ang barko dahil hindi alam ng OOW ang ECDIS, echo sounder, gyro at Inmarsat. Sinusuri ang kaalaman, hindi lang ang gamit.
i: Type-specific ECDIS training for Master and all OOWs. Each OOW can show: safety contour/depth, alarms, route check, ENC update status, chart permits.
Type-specific ECDIS training ng Master at lahat ng OOW. Kayang ipakita ng OOW: safety contour/depth, alarm, route check, ENC update, chart permit.

ENCs/charts updated for Canadian waters; Canadian Notices to Mariners (Annual + monthly), Sailing Directions, Radio Aids to Marine Navigation, Canadian Tide & Current Tables, List of Lights. Ask agent for the Canadian charts/pubs list.
Updated ang ENC/chart para sa Canada; Canadian Notices to Mariners (Annual + monthly), Sailing Directions, Radio Aids, Canadian Tide & Current Tables, List of Lights. Humingi ng listahan sa agent.
Includes pilot boarding, MCTS reporting points, ECA boundary/fuel changeover point, UKC, whale zones (NARW Gulf of St. Lawrence / ECHO Haro Strait), NAVWARNs.
Kasama ang pilot boarding, MCTS reporting points, ECA boundary/changeover point, UKC, whale zones (NARW / ECHO Haro Strait), NAVWARN.
Both radars + ARPA working; gyro & magnetic compass errors recorded each watch; deviation card current; echo sounder recording.
Gumagana ang 2 radar + ARPA; naka-record ang gyro at compass error bawat watch; updated ang deviation card; nagre-record ang echo sounder.
Draught, destination, nav status updated. Transport Canada checks speed limits from AIS and asks the Master for an explanation.
Updated ang draught, destination, nav status. Sinusuri ng Transport Canada ang bilis mula sa AIS at magtatanong sa Master.
Annual Performance Test certificate valid; any earlier repair/dispensation formally closed with class/flag.
Valid ang Annual Performance Test certificate; sarado nang pormal sa class/flag ang dating repair/dispensation.
Switched on at sea, not by-passed, tested.
Naka-on sa dagat, walang bypass, na-test.
All lights burn with correct coloured globes (no white globes painted red/green), spare bulbs, shapes, daylight signal lamp, whistle.
Gumagana lahat ng ilaw na may tamang kulay (bawal ang puting bombilya na pininturahan), may spare, shapes, daylight signal lamp, whistle.
Daily/weekly/monthly tests logged; battery load test; NAVTEX; EPIRB annual test + shore-based maintenance certificate; SARTs; portable VHF primary batteries in date; GOC endorsements for all.
Naka-log ang daily/weekly/monthly test; battery load test; NAVTEX; EPIRB annual test + shore-based maintenance; SART; valid ang primary battery ng portable VHF; GOC endorsement ng lahat.
LRIT conformance test report on board; SSAS tested and recorded.
May LRIT conformance test report; na-test at naka-record ang SSAS.
Pre-departure tests logged (12 h before sailing); emergency steering drill every 3 months logged.
Naka-log ang pre-departure test (12 h bago umalis); emergency steering drill kada 3 buwan.
Clear-view screens/wipers/window heating working; bridge heating; searchlights ready.
Gumagana ang clear-view screen/wiper/window heating; bridge heating; handa ang searchlight.

why: Wrong or old certificates are the quickest way to a deficiency. After a class change, the old certificates must leave the file.
Mali o lumang certificate ang pinakamabilis na deficiency. Pagkatapos magpalit ng class, alisin ang lumang certificate sa file.
i: Originals of the current class/statutory set in the certificate file; old (superseded) certificates removed and archived so nobody shows the wrong one.
Orihinal ng kasalukuyang set sa file; alisin at i-archive ang luma para walang magpakita ng mali.
Any SOLAS exemption (e.g. II-2/10.7.1.3 no fixed gas in holds) with its cargo-list annex on board; cargo must be on the list; validity checked.
May SOLAS exemption (hal. II-2/10.7.1.3) kasama ang cargo-list annex; dapat nasa listahan ang cargo; valid.
CSR updated for any class/DOC/owner change. PSCOs compare it with the certificates.
Updated ang CSR sa anumang palit ng class/DOC/owner. Ikukumpara ito ng PSCO sa certificates.
DOC copy + SMC, ISSC + SSP, MLC certificate + DMLC Part I & II. Dates and names match.
DOC copy + SMC, ISSC + SSP, MLC certificate + DMLC I at II. Tugma ang petsa at pangalan.
Crew list matches the Safe Manning Document in number and rank.
Tugma ang crew list sa Safe Manning Document sa bilang at rank.
CoCs + flag endorsements, medicals, STCW basic/advanced courses, ratings' watchkeeping certificates — check every expiry before arrival.
CoC + flag endorsement, medical, STCW courses, watchkeeping certificate ng ratings — suriin ang expiry bago dumating.
Document of Authorization for grain + grain loading booklet; loading manual; loading instrument annual test record.
Document of Authorization + grain loading booklet; loading manual; annual test ng loading instrument.
Approved CSM on board. CIC on Cargo Securing runs until 30/11/2026 — the questionnaire may be asked.
Approved CSM sa barko. CIC Cargo Securing hanggang 30/11/2026 — maaaring itanong.
Oil Record Book Part I, Garbage Record Book, Ballast Water Record Book, ODS record book, fuel changeover log — entries complete and signed.
ORB Part I, GRB, BWRB, ODS record book, fuel changeover log — kumpleto at pirmado.
IAPP + Record of Construction, EIAPP & NOx Technical Files for all engines, IEE, SEEMP Part III, DCS Statement of Compliance and CII rating.
IAPP + Record of Construction, EIAPP at NOx Technical File ng lahat ng makina, IEE, SEEMP III, DCS SoC at CII rating.
Ballast Water Management Certificate (D-2), approved BWM Plan, BWMS type approval certificate.
BWM Certificate (D-2), approved BWM Plan, type approval certificate ng BWMS.
Approved SOPEP with updated contact list (Canadian authorities via agent); Garbage Management Plan; placards posted.
Approved SOPEP na updated ang contact (Canadian authorities sa agent); Garbage Management Plan; may placard.
P&I, Bunker Convention and Wreck Removal certificates on board and valid.
Valid na P&I, Bunker Convention at Wreck Removal certificate sa barko.
Certificate of Test & Thorough Examination (provision, ER and bunker cranes) + Register of Lifting Appliances.
Certificate of Test & Thorough Examination (provision, ER, bunker crane) + Register of Lifting Appliances.
Last PSC reports on board — every item closed with evidence and flag/class close-out.
Nasa barko ang huling PSC report — sarado lahat na may ebidensya at close-out ng flag/class.
Liferafts & HRUs, fire extinguishers, CO2 system, BA compressor air quality (3-monthly), EEBDs, lifeboat & rescue boat on-load release gear (annual / 5-yearly).
Liferaft at HRU, extinguisher, CO2, BA compressor air quality (3 buwan), EEBD, on-load release gear (taunan / 5 taon).
SSCEC valid (6 months); medicine chest inspected and certificate valid.
Ship Sanitation Certificate at medical chest
Valid ang SSCEC (6 buwan); na-inspect ang medicine chest at valid ang certificate.
Muster list shows the present crew; drills, training and new-joiner familiarisation recorded.
Kasalukuyang crew ang nasa muster list; naka-record ang drill, training at familiarisation.

t: Crew, MLC at kondisyon ng tirahan
why: Canadian PSCOs ask who has been on board more than 11 months. Crew complaints go straight to Transport Canada.
Tinatanong ng Canadian PSCO kung sino ang lampas 11 buwan sa barko. Diretso sa Transport Canada ang reklamo ng crew.
i: Signed, valid, correct shipowner name on every SEA (also on extensions); no old class/company details.
Pirmado, valid, tamang pangalan ng shipowner sa bawat SEA (pati extension); walang lumang detalye.
Nobody over 11 months on board on arrival in Canada (MLC). Arrange reliefs in time with the office.
Walang lampas 11 buwan sa barko pagdating sa Canada (MLC). Ayusin ang relief kasama ang office.
Wage accounts/pay slips available; on-board complaint procedure posted with contacts; CBA copy on board.
May wage account/pay slip; nakapaskil ang complaint procedure at contact; may kopya ng CBA.
Records complete and true; match the log book, drills and cargo times.
Kumpleto at totoo; tugma sa log book, drill at oras ng cargo.
UV sterilizer working; water analysis and tank cleaning recorded.
Gumagana ang UV sterilizer; naka-record ang water analysis at tank cleaning.
Clean, cold rooms with temperature log, food enough for the voyage, Master's weekly inspection records.
Malinis, may temperature log ang cold room, sapat ang pagkain, may weekly inspection ng Master.
All faucets, showers, toilets and drains working (Quebec 2025 detention included broken faucets and hospital shower). Hospital clean, not used as store.
Gumagana lahat ng gripo, shower, toilet at drain (Quebec 2025: sirang gripo at hospital shower). Malinis ang hospital, hindi bodega.
Cabins clean, AC/heating working, no extension cords or private heaters, laundry working.
Malinis ang cabin, gumagana ang AC/heater, walang extension cord o sariling heater, gumagana ang laundry.
PPE issued and recorded; Drug & Alcohol policy and test records.
Naka-record ang PPE; may Drug & Alcohol policy at test record.

why: Fire safety is the No.1 detainable area worldwide (ClassNK 2025: 426). Fire doors, dampers, emergency fire pump and crew knowledge are always tested.
Fire safety ang #1 detainable sa mundo (ClassNK 2025: 426). Laging sinusuri ang fire door, damper, emergency fire pump at kaalaman ng crew.
i: Every fire door closes and latches by itself. No hooks, wedges or ropes holding them open (Quebec 2025 detention).
Kusang sumasara at nagla-latch ang bawat fire door. Walang hook, kalang o lubid (Quebec 2025 detention).
All operate freely, open/close marked, no holes from corrosion, gaskets OK, not blocked by stores.
Malayang gumagalaw, may marka open/close, walang butas, OK ang gasket, hindi harang ng gamit.
Starts and gives good pressure at two hydrants on deck quickly; suction/priming OK; start instructions posted.
Umaandar at may magandang pressure sa 2 hydrant agad; OK ang suction/priming; may instructions.
Pressure gauges working, isolation valve operates, no leaking pipes or hydrants.
Main fire pump at fire main
Gumagana ang gauge, ang isolation valve, walang tagas sa tubo o hydrant.
Boxes complete: hose, dual-purpose nozzle, spanner; couplings fit; no leaks.
Kumpleto: hose, dual-purpose nozzle, spanner; tugma ang coupling; walang tagas.
No faults/disabled loops; detector test log up to date.
Walang fault/disabled loop; updated ang test log ng detector.
Cylinder weights recorded, release alarm works, operating instructions posted — and officers can explain the release sequence (Vancouver 2025: 3/O did not know CO2 operation).
Naka-record ang timbang, gumagana ang release alarm, may instructions — at kayang ipaliwanag ng officers ang release (Vancouver 2025: hindi alam ng 3/O).
Fixed system complete and piping not wasted (Quebec 2025 detention: perforated sprinkler line).
Kumpleto ang fixed system at walang butas ang tubo (Quebec 2025: butas na sprinkler line).
Complete sets to the current standard (EN 469:2020 Level 2, SOLAS/MED).
Kumpletong set ayon sa kasalukuyang standard (EN 469:2020 Level 2, SOLAS/MED).
Cylinders full, spares charged; crew can don SCBA and check pressure & low-pressure whistle (Vancouver 2025). EEBD number as per fire plan.
Puno ang cylinder at spare; kayang isuot ng crew ang SCBA at suriin ang pressure at whistle (Vancouver 2025). EEBD ayon sa fire plan.
In place as per fire plan, charged, service labels in date, brackets OK.
Nasa lugar ayon sa fire plan, may karga, valid ang label, OK ang bracket.
QCVs close from remote, air reservoir charged. Emergency generator tank QCV directly on the tank (no spool piece). Fan/pump remote stops tested.
Sumasara ang QCV mula remote, may hangin ang reservoir. QCV ng em'cy gen tank direkta sa tangke (walang spool piece). Na-test ang remote stop.
Section valves correct and system tested.
Tama ang section valves at na-test ang system.
Hood and duct clean (no grease), fire blanket, extinguisher, damper working.
Malinis ang hood at duct (walang grasa), may fire blanket, extinguisher, gumagana ang damper.
Matches equipment on board; copy in weathertight box outside accommodation; International Shore Connection available.
Tugma sa gamit; may kopya sa weathertight box sa labas; may International Shore Connection.
Free, unlocked from inside, signs and emergency lighting working (Vancouver 2025 detention: ER escape locked).
Malaya, bukas mula sa loob, gumagana ang signs at emergency light (Vancouver 2025: naka-lock ang ER escape).

why: LSA is the No.2 detainable area. In Canada lifeboat engines and davits are run in front of the PSCO (Quebec 2025: both boat engines failed + davit cradle stuck).
LSA ang #2 detainable. Sa Canada, pinapaandar ang lifeboat engine at davit sa harap ng PSCO (Quebec 2025: parehong makina bigo + stuck ang cradle).
i: Start cold, ahead/astern, fuel full, batteries charged. Run weekly and log.
Umaandar nang malamig, ahead/astern, puno ang fuel, may karga ang battery. Patakbuhin lingguhan at i-log.
Brakes, limit switches, no hydraulic leaks, swing-out under reserve power, cradles not stuck.
Brake, limit switch, walang hydraulic leak, nakaka-swing-out sa reserve power, hindi stuck ang cradle.
Hooks fully reset, indicators in 'closed' position, annual / 5-yearly service certificates on board.
Buo ang reset ng hook, 'closed' ang indicator, may annual / 5-taon na service certificate.
Inventory complete and in date (water, rations, pyros, first aid), windows intact, bilge pump, lights.
Kumpleto at valid (tubig, rasyon, pyro, first aid), buo ang bintana, bilge pump, ilaw.
Engine starts, equipment complete, davit controls tested; any dispensation closed.
Umaandar ang makina, kumpleto ang gamit, na-test ang davit control; sarado ang dispensation.
Service and HRU dates valid, painter with weak link correctly fixed, embarkation ladders OK.
Valid ang service at HRU, tama ang painter at weak link, OK ang embarkation ladder.
Number as per plan, self-igniting lights & smoke signals in date, retro tape, ship's name.
Bilang ayon sa plan, valid ang light at smoke signal, may retro tape at pangalan ng barko.
Correct number, lights/whistles OK, suits air-tested; stowage marked.
Tamang bilang, OK ang ilaw/whistle, na-air-test ang suit; may marka ang lalagyan.
Ladders maintained (Quebec 2025 deficiency); muster/embarkation stations lit, IMO signs, instructions posted.
Maayos ang ladder (Quebec 2025); may ilaw ang muster/embarkation station, IMO signs, instructions.
Training manual in mess rooms and recreation room; maintenance instructions available.
Training manual sa mess at recreation room; may maintenance instructions.

t: Main deck, hatch covers, holds & load line
Main deck, hatch cover, holds at load line
why: Weathertightness is a 'structure' item: holed air pipes, missing manhole bolts or wasted hatch coamings lead straight to detention (Quebec area 2025: No.4 hatch coaming perforated).
Ang weathertightness ay 'structure': butas na air pipe, kulang na bolt ng manhole o kinakalawang na coaming = detention (Quebec 2025: butas ang No.4 coaming).
i: Rubber packing, compression bars, cleats, drain channels & non-return valves OK; chalk/ultrasonic test record.
OK ang rubber packing, compression bar, cleat, drain channel at non-return valve; may chalk/ultrasonic test record.
No hydraulic oil leaks on cylinders, hoses, valves (Vancouver 2025 detention). Clean any old oil on deck.
Walang tagas ng hydraulic oil sa cylinder, hose, valve (Vancouver 2025). Linisin ang lumang langis sa deck.
No wastage, holes or cracks; coaming brackets complete.
Walang kalawang, butas o bitak; kumpleto ang bracket.
Floats/flaps free, gaskets OK, heads not holed, marked with tank name.
Malaya ang float/flap, OK ang gasket, walang butas, may pangalan ng tangke.
Caps in place, chained, threads OK.
Nasa lugar ang takip, may kadena, OK ang thread.
Closing devices work, dogs and gaskets OK, marked open/closed.
Gumagana ang closing device, OK ang dogs at gasket, may marka open/closed.
All bolts fitted on fuel/ballast manholes (check after any yard work).
Kumpleto ang bolt sa fuel/ballast manhole (suriin pagkatapos ng yard).
Each hold alarm and pre-alarm tested and recorded; no active alarms; sensors clean (after blasting/cleaning).
Na-test at naka-record ang alarm at pre-alarm ng bawat hold; walang aktibong alarm; malinis ang sensor.
Grit/abrasive swept out, no loose scale or flaking paint, bilge wells clean, burlap ready. Grain loading needs Transport Canada 'Readiness to Load' and CFIA hold inspection.
Walang grit/abrasive, walang maluwag na kalawang o natutuklap na pintura, malinis ang bilge well, handa ang burlap. Kailangan ng TC 'Readiness to Load' at CFIA inspection.
Ladders, platforms, manhole covers intact and secured.
Buo at secured ang ladder, platform at manhole cover.
Junction boxes closed, cables and pipes on brackets, deck lights watertight (earth faults often come from deck lights after washing).
Sarado ang junction box, nasa bracket ang kable at tubo, watertight ang deck light (madalas ang earth fault mula sa ilaw pagkatapos maghugas).
Rails and guard chains complete (monkey island), mast stays and wire terminations secured.
Kumpleto ang rail at guard chain (monkey island), secured ang mast stay at wire termination.
Emergency towing procedure on board and equipment location known (Vancouver 2025: equipment not found).
May emergency towing procedure at alam kung nasaan ang gamit (Vancouver 2025: hindi nakita).
Spill kit complete, scupper plugs, drip trays clean and dry.
Kumpleto ang spill kit, scupper plug, malinis at tuyo ang drip tray.

why: Since 2024 SOLAS II-1/3-8 requires a Mooring System Management Plan and documented inspection of lines and equipment.
Mula 2024, kailangan ng SOLAS II-1/3-8 ang Mooring System Management Plan at naka-dokumentong inspection ng lines at gamit.
i: Brakes in order, brake test records (company form), no oil leaks, guards in place.
Maayos ang brake, may brake test record, walang tagas, may guard.
Condition, certificates, line records per mooring plan / MSMP.
Kondisyon, certificate, record ayon sa mooring plan / MSMP.
Bitter end secured, chain locker cover and spurling pipe covers closed.
Secured ang bitter end, sarado ang chain locker at spurling pipe cover.

why: Oil in the bilges, hot surfaces, a by-passed OWS or a crew that cannot run their own equipment are classic detentions in Canada.
Langis sa bilge, mainit na surface, bypass na OWS o crew na hindi kaya ang sariling gamit = klasikong detention sa Canada.
i: No oil on tank tops, bilges, drip trays; no oily rags; save-alls empty.
Walang langis sa tank top, bilge, drip tray; walang basahang may langis; walang laman ang save-all.
No fuel/lube leaks (Quebec 2025: leaking fuel pump); HP fuel pipe jackets and spray screens fitted.
Tagas ng main at aux engine
Walang tagas ng fuel/lube (Quebec 2025: tumutulong fuel pump); may jacket ang HP fuel pipe at spray screen.
All surfaces >220 °C insulated; no oil-soaked lagging; lagging removed for repairs put back.
Naka-insulate lahat ng >220 °C; walang lagging na may langis; ibinalik ang tinanggal na lagging.
Parameter records complete for all engines (Quebec 2025: missing DG entries); NOx component IDs match Technical File.
Kumpleto ang parameter record ng lahat ng makina (Quebec 2025: kulang ang DG); tugma ang NOx ID sa Technical File.
Engineers can demonstrate the OWS and 15 ppm alarm/stop; calibration certificate; no flexible hoses, no by-pass, piping as per IOPP drawing (Vancouver 2025 detention).
Kayang ipakita ng engineers ang OWS at 15 ppm alarm/stop; may calibration certificate; walang flexible hose, walang bypass, tubo ayon sa IOPP drawing (Vancouver 2025).
ORB matches soundings and IOPP Form A tanks; sludge pump and standard discharge connection; incinerator records.
Tugma ang ORB sa sounding at IOPP Form A; sludge pump at standard discharge connection; incinerator record.
Starts automatically on blackout and takes load; fuel tank QCV directly on tank; room clean; batteries/charger OK.
Kusang umaandar sa blackout at may load; QCV direkta sa tangke; malinis ang kuwarto; OK ang battery/charger.
Emergency lights work; battery room ventilated, charger OK.
Gumagana ang emergency light; may bentilasyon ang battery room, OK ang charger.
Emergency steering instructions & block diagram posted, gyro repeater, communications to bridge; crew practised (Vancouver 2025 detention).
May emergency steering instructions at block diagram, gyro repeater, komunikasyon sa bridge; nag-practice ang crew (Vancouver 2025).
Bilge pumps and high-level alarms tested.
Na-test ang bilge pump at high-level alarm.
Running correctly; UV/chlorination working, sight glasses not blanked (Quebec 2025); type matches ISPP certificate.
Tama ang andar; gumagana ang UV/chlorination, walang takip ang sight glass (Quebec 2025); tugma sa ISPP.
Operational, no alarms, filters/UV/TRO OK, records kept, engineers can operate it in front of PSCO.
Gumagana, walang alarm, OK ang filter/UV/TRO, may record, kaya ng engineers sa harap ng PSCO.
Insulation readings, no earth faults, panels closed, rubber mats in place.
May insulation reading, walang earth fault, sarado ang panel, may rubber mat.
Grinder guards/eye shields; O2/acetylene with flashback arrestors, gauges OK, cylinders secured.
May guard/eye shield ang grinder; O2/acetylene na may flashback arrestor, OK ang gauge, secured ang cylinder.
Escape trunk unlocked and lit, self-closing door works; skylight/funnel flaps close.
Bukas at may ilaw ang escape trunk, gumagana ang self-closing door; sumasara ang skylight/funnel flap.
No over-ridden alarms; UMS alarm tests logged; hydraulic power packs clean.
Walang naka-override na alarm; naka-log ang UMS alarm test; malinis ang hydraulic power pack.
System to prevent sea-chest icing/choking available (St. Lawrence winter rules). Check ship is on Transport Canada's compliant list (winternav@tc.gc.ca).
May system laban sa yelo sa sea chest (winter rules ng St. Lawrence). Suriin kung nasa compliant list ng Transport Canada (winternav@tc.gc.ca).

t: Pollution prevention at Canadian environmental rules
why: Canada enforces the North American ECA, its own Ballast Water Regulations (SOR/2021-120) and whale-protection speed measures.
Ipinapatupad ng Canada ang North American ECA, sariling Ballast Water Regulations (SOR/2021-120) at speed limits para sa balyena.
i: 0.10% S fuel before entering the North American ECA (200 nm); changeover time, position and tank volumes logged; BDNs kept 3 years with MARPOL samples.
0.10% S bago pumasok sa North American ECA (200 nm); naka-log ang oras, posisyon at dami; BDN 3 taon kasama ang MARPOL sample.
BWMS used for every discharge; BWRB complete; ballast water report sent before arrival through the agent; sediment management recorded.
Gamitin ang BWMS sa bawat discharge; kumpleto ang BWRB; ipinadala ang ballast report bago dumating; naka-record ang sediment.
If ballast will be discharged in Canadian fresh waters, check the extra measures of SOR/2021-120 with the agent before arrival.
Kung magdi-discharge sa fresh water ng Canada, suriin ang dagdag na measures ng SOR/2021-120 sa agent bago dumating.
Segregated bins & placards; GRB up to date; no plastics overboard; foreign food waste landed only through the agent's approved contractor.
Hiwalay na bins at placard; updated ang GRB; bawal plastic sa dagat; foreign food waste sa approved contractor lang.
No discharge of untreated sewage; any discharge must leave no visible solids, film or sheen (Canadian regulations).
Bawal ang untreated sewage; walang makikitang solids, film o sheen (Canadian regulations).
Gulf of St. Lawrence NARW speed zones (10 kn when triggered) and ECHO voluntary slowdown Haro Strait/Boundary Pass (11 kn for bulkers, until 30/11/2026). Log compliance.
NARW speed zones sa Gulf of St. Lawrence (10 kn kapag may alerto) at ECHO slowdown sa Haro Strait/Boundary Pass (11 kn, hanggang 30/11/2026). I-log.
AFS certificate/declaration on board; hull paint not peeling.
May AFS certificate/declaration; hindi natutuklap ang pintura.
Restricted areas locked/marked; visitors escorted; search records.
Naka-lock/may marka ang restricted area; may escort ang bisita; may search record.
Last 10 port calls, Declarations of Security, security drills & training, SSAS test.
Huling 10 port call, DoS, security drill at training, SSAS test.

drills: Fire drill — ER fire
Realistic scenario with smoke location; boundary cooling; ventilation & fuel shut-off; SCBA team checks pressure; communications Master → team leader → bridge. Talk through CO2 release step by step.
Vancouver 2025: Master & crew unfamiliar with firefighting systems; poor communication.
Fire drill — sunog sa ER
Makatotohanang scenario; boundary cooling; patayin ang ventilation at fuel; sinusuri ng SCBA team ang pressure; komunikasyon Master → team leader → bridge. Ipaliwanag ang CO2 release hakbang-hakbang.
Abandon ship
Crew at muster in 2 min with lifejackets & immersion suits; boat lowered (if allowed), engine started, run ahead/astern.
Quebec 2025: both boat engines failed; davit stuck.
Abandon ship
Crew sa muster sa loob ng 2 min na may lifejacket at immersion suit; ibaba ang boat (kung pwede), paandarin, ahead/astern.
Emergency steering
Change-over to local control, communication with bridge, gyro repeater read-back.
Vancouver 2025: crew unfamiliar with emergency steering.
Emergency steering
Lipat sa local control, komunikasyon sa bridge, basahin ang gyro repeater.
Enclosed space rescue
Permit, gas test, rescue equipment, tripod/stretcher. (CIC 2027 = Enclosed Space Entry.)
Common ISM/drill finding.
Enclosed space rescue
Permit, gas test, rescue equipment, tripod/stretcher. (CIC 2027 = Enclosed Space Entry.)
Blackout & emergency generator
Simulate blackout; emergency generator on load; emergency fire pump start.
Emergency systems = No.3 detainable area.
Blackout at emergency generator
Simulate ang blackout; em'cy gen may load; paandarin ang emergency fire pump.
OWS demonstration
2/E runs the OWS, shows 15 ppm alarm and automatic stop.
Vancouver 2025: officer could not operate OWS.
OWS demonstration
Pinapaandar ng 2/E ang OWS, ipinapakita ang 15 ppm alarm at automatic stop.
ECDIS / bridge equipment
Each OOW shows the PSCO the ECDIS settings, radar, echo sounder, gyro, GMDSS.
Vancouver 2025: OOW not familiar with equipment.
ECDIS / bridge equipment
Bawat OOW ipinapakita sa PSCO ang ECDIS settings, radar, echo sounder, gyro, GMDSS.
Oil spill (SOPEP)
Spill on deck during bunkering: plugs, absorbents, reporting to Canadian Coast Guard via the contact list.
Canadian pollution focus.
Oil spill (SOPEP)
Tapon sa deck habang bunkering: plug, absorbent, report sa Canadian Coast Guard ayon sa contact list.
golden: Master or C/O meets the PSCO at the gangway; ship's particulars, crew list and certificates ready in one file.
Sasalubungin ng Master o C/O ang PSCO sa gangway; handa sa isang file ang particulars, crew list at certificates.
Escort the PSCO all the time with an officer who takes notes and photos of anything mentioned.
Laging may kasamang officer ang PSCO na nagsusulat at kumukuha ng litrato.
Answer honestly and briefly. Never argue in front of the crew. If you don't know, say you will check — then check.
Sumagot nang tapat at maikli. Huwag makipagtalo sa harap ng crew. Kung hindi alam, sabihing susuriin — at suriin.
A defect already reported to office/class with a repair plan is treated better than a hidden one.
Mas maganda ang trato sa sirang naka-report na may repair plan kaysa sa itinago.
Let the crew do their own job in drills — the PSCO is testing them, not the Master.
Hayaan ang crew sa sariling trabaho sa drill — sila ang sinusubok ng PSCO.
Read the PSC report (Form A/B) carefully before signing; check codes and texts. Ask the action code of each item (e.g. 17 = before departure, 30 = detention).
Basahin nang mabuti ang PSC report (Form A/B) bago pumirma; suriin ang code at text. Itanong ang action code (17 = bago umalis, 30 = detention).
Send the report to the office immediately — same hour.
Ipadala agad sa office ang report — sa loob ng isang oras.

Specific Hatch Cover Inspection and Maintenance

Cargo hold entry and emergency response
Cargo hold ventilation and dew-point / 3-degree rule
Engine room critical equipment and emergencies
Visitor / inspector safety familiarization (emergency briefing, signed)
Visitors & inspectors (briefed by OOW / Safety Officer)

Crew training and familiarization records verified
Outstanding items and target completion dates identified

il.t: RightShip inspector's list (as used on board)
il.v: RISQ 3.2 · Dry bulk · inspector's own document & check list, in his order
r: 📄 Documents (all papers – this list from top)
🤝 Back up top for the closing meeting
i: Last 10 ports of call and cargo loaded
Latest Class Status Report (not more than 7 days before the inspection)
Class Certificate / IOPP / DOC / SMC (if applicable)
Ballast Water Management Cert (2020/10/28 MEPC.300(72)) / Annual report
Document of Compliance for the Carriage of Dangerous Goods / IMSBC Code / Grain
Continuous Synopsis Record | New Manager taken over / Unscheduled repair
Latest Enhanced Survey / Condition Evaluation Report
PSC inspection report in last 12 months
Is the vessel manager a subscriber to Dry Bulk Centre of Excellence (DBCE)?
Has a DryBMS (Dry Bulk Management Standard) Self-Assessment been completed?
P&I Certificate of Entry | Certificate of Financial Security
Cert. of 120 t SWL bollard on aft deck (if vessel DWT over 120,000)
Type approval Cert. of EGCS – Open or Closed loop (5 year verify)
Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan (SEEMP) Part I/II/III and CoC
Fuel consumption report / Carbon Intensity Indicator CII data / rating
EEDI/EEXI Technical File – EEXI-R / A | EPL / OMM / release time taken record
Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan (SOPEP) | Emergency Towing Booklet (10.22)
Bio-fouling Management Plan and record book
Stability booklet & Loading Manual | Cargo Securing Manual
Elevator annual service inspection (if fitted) | Maintenance risk assessment / PTW
Gas detectors last calibration – calibration / bump test record
Specific gas detector for specific cargo (CO2) / cargo assessment
